before.title: 1.6 CDTi Timing Chain Tensioner Failure and Chain Stretch (B16DTH/B16DTE/B16DTL)
before.description: The 'whisper diesel' 1.6 CDTi engines fitted to the Zafira Tourer C suffer a well-documented timing chain failure. The original chain tensioner lacks a gasket, so oil drains out of the tensioner when the engine is switched off. This produces a metallic rattle/ticking on cold start (typically 2-5 seconds) as the chain runs slack before oil pressure builds. Over time the chain stretches, the plastic guides wear, and in severe cases the chain can jump timing or snap, causing pistons to contact valves and destroying the engine. Failures are commonly reported well before 100,000 miles. The chain is at the rear of the engine (gearbox side), making it a labour-intensive repair.
before.solution: Replace the timing chain, both sprockets, guides and the uprated/gasketed tensioner as a kit (10-12 hours labour, often requiring engine/gearbox separation). Catch it early at the first cold-start rattle. Frequent oil changes with the correct dexos2 spec oil at 6,000-9,000 mile intervals slow chain wear. If the chain has already snapped, expect a full engine rebuild or replacement.
symptoms: Metallic rattle or ticking on cold start
Rattle from gearbox end of engine

before.title: 1.8 Petrol (Z18XER/A18XER) Coolant Leaks and Water Pump Failure
before.description: The 1.8 16V petrol engine (Z18XER, later A18XER) in the Zafira B is prone to coolant leaks. The water pump seal fails and weeps coolant from the pump pulley area (sometimes spraying onto the air-con compressor), and the plastic coolant pipes/housings and ageing hoses crack and seep. Owners also report the oil cooler/cooler seal weeping. If unnoticed the car loses coolant and can overheat. Note this engine is timing-BELT driven (not chain), so the belt and tensioner/water pump should be serviced together to avoid belt failure causing valve damage.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system to pinpoint the leak. Replace the water pump (ideally with the timing belt and tensioner as a combined job, ~every 60k miles / belt interval), and renew cracked plastic coolant pipes, the thermostat housing and any perished hoses. Inspect the oil cooler seal. Use the correct long-life coolant.
symptoms: Coolant leak under car / low coolant level
Coolant spray around water pump pulley
Visible weeping from plastic coolant pipes

before.title: 1.9 CDTi Swirl Flap (Drallklappen) Linkage Failure (Z19DTH/Z19DT)
before.description: The 1.9 CDTi engines in the Zafira B use intake-manifold swirl flaps controlled by a plastic actuator linkage. The linkage rod and bushings wear or break, so the flaps no longer move correctly, triggering limp mode and stored fault codes P2279 (intake air system leak) and/or P2075 (intake manifold runner position sensor/switch). German owners (motor-talk.de, zafira-forum.de) report this commonly around 90,000-150,000 km, often alongside EGR and DPF clogging on the same engine. Left unrepaired, a flap can break off and be ingested by the engine.
before.solution: Fit a swirl flap linkage repair kit (replacement rod, bushings and clips) — a low-cost fix that restores flap movement; clear codes afterwards. Some owners delete/blank the swirl flaps where legal. Inspect and clean the EGR valve and intake at the same time, as carbon build-up worsens the problem.

before.title: Zafira B Fire Risk — HVAC Blower Resistor (2015-2016 Recall)
before.description: Vauxhall/Opel issued a major safety recall in 2015-2016 for Zafira B (Mk2, 2005-2014) after dozens of vehicles caught fire. The blower-motor resistor pre-resistor and associated wiring could overheat and ignite. Many owners reported repeat fires after the initial recall fix; a second improved recall followed.
before.solution: Check VIN against Vauxhall/Opel recall database — both R/2015/116 and the follow-up action. If unsure whether your car has had BOTH fixes, request paperwork. Do not run the blower on continuous high if recall status is unknown.

proposal.title: Zafira B Fire Risk — HVAC Blower Resistor (2015-2016 Recall)
proposal.description: Official DVSA bulletin NCA/2015/026 covers right-hand-drive Vauxhall Zafira B model years 2005-2014 and states that an overheated heater-fan resistor can create a fire risk if the failed thermal fuse is manipulated or bypassed. Vauxhall then issued a second safety recall, 16-C-050, for Zafira B vehicles with manual air conditioning or without air conditioning, including vehicles already repaired under 15-C-097, because the resistor could degrade under specific circumstances and lead to fire.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN and heating/air-conditioning configuration with Vauxhall and complete every outstanding recall free of charge. The official second-recall repair uses a wax-fuse heater-fan resistor and water deflector and checks the blower motor for replacement. Until that repair, follow the current manufacturer instruction for the exact vehicle; the 2016 letter specifies fan setting 0 or 4 and setting 0 if speed 4 does not operate. Never bypass a thermal fuse. Do not buy or install a resistor, motor or wiring repair from this page; recall status and the authorized remedy are VIN-specific.
symptoms: fan-speed loss treated as a recall warning
affectedSystems: heater fan resistor and thermal fuse

before.title: Electric Power Steering (Delphi EPS) Column Unit Failure
before.description: Zafira B models fitted with the Delphi/GM electric power steering (EPS) column-mounted unit commonly lose power assistance, often in both directions. The torque/position sensor inside the column-integrated EPS motor unit degrades, and the system stores fault code C1500 (Torque Position Sensor). The fault frequently starts intermittently — assistance cuts out briefly then returns — before becoming permanent, leaving the steering very heavy and hard to turn. This is a recognised failure of the EPS control unit/sensor rather than a hydraulic pump or fluid issue.
before.solution: Diagnose via stored code (C1500). The EPS column unit can be remanufactured/repaired (sensor and electronics rebuilt) by specialists at lower cost than a new genuine unit, or replaced with a new column. Reset/relearn the steering angle sensor after fitment. Check connector and wiring integrity first, as poor connections can mimic the fault.
symptoms: Heavy / hard steering in both directions
Intermittent loss of assist that later becomes permanent

before.title: Front Suspension Control Arm Bolt Corrosion / Breakage (KBA Recall 15411R)
before.description: Later Zafira Tourer/Life models (and related Vivaro vans on the same platform) built between 23 September 2020 and 30 June 2022 were recalled because corrosion of the front suspension control-arm bushing area can cause the control-arm mounting bolt to break. A broken bolt leads to sudden unpredictable handling and potential loss of vehicle control. Around 76,778 vehicles were covered by the German KBA campaign (references 15411R/15414R/15415R).
before.solution: Under the recall, an authorised workshop replaces the screws/bolts and bushings on both sides of the front control arms. Owners should check recall status by VIN and have the work done before further driving if a clunk or handling change is noticed at the front.

before.title: NOx Sensor / SCR System Failure on Euro 6 Diesels (Zafira Tourer C)
before.description: Euro 6 diesel Zafira Tourer C models with SCR/AdBlue (1.6 CDTi B16DTH and 2.0 CDTi B20DTH/D20DTH) commonly suffer NOx sensor failure. The upstream/downstream NOx sensors degrade and report implausible values, setting catalyst-efficiency and NOx-sensor codes (e.g. P20EE, P229F, P118B) and putting the car into reduced power / limp mode with an emissions warning and a restart countdown in some cases. German owners (motor-talk.de) report this as a known fault from around 80,000 km. NOx sensors are relatively expensive genuine parts and often fail again if cheap aftermarket units are used.
before.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool to identify which NOx sensor (position 1 upstream or position 2 downstream) and confirm the SCR catalyst is functioning. Replace the failed NOx sensor with an OE-quality part and clear codes. Verify AdBlue/DEF quality and dosing, and rule out a genuinely degraded SCR catalyst before condemning the sensor.

before.title: Steering Column Intermediate Shaft Loose Press-Fit (Safety Recall R/2010/032)
before.description: Zafira B vehicles built between 16 November 2009 and 24 March 2010 were recalled because the steering column intermediate shaft can have a loose press fit on the upper joint yoke. Over time this develops increasing free play and a knocking noise from the steering column; if ignored, it can ultimately lead to loss of steering control. Approximately 8,854 UK cars were affected under DVSA recall R/2010/032 (launched May 2010). This is a separate, later steering recall to the earlier steering-wheel-controls campaign.
before.solution: Have a new intermediate steering shaft fitted under the manufacturer recall (free of charge). Check the recall status by VIN with an Opel/Vauxhall dealer; any car with knocking or play in the column from this build window should be inspected before further driving.
symptoms: Risk of loss of steering control
